findings.title: Global group canManage() grants manage rights for VIEW permission
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returns true when the caller has either VIEW or MANAGE on the all-groups resource (hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)). This method is used by GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup through requireManage(), so a principal granted only the Groups view scope can create or move top-level groups. The global manage check should require MANAGE only.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns authorization resource IDs instead of group IDs
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() adds groupResource.getId() to the returned set. Callers such as UsersResource.searchForUser and getUsersCount expect realm group IDs and pass this set to user search/count queries via UserModel.GROUPS. The authorization resource ID is not the group ID (the group ID is stored as the resource name), so user searches and counts restricted by group-view permissions will filter on wrong IDs, producing missing or incorrect results and breaking pagination.

findings.title: Group-type resource is processed as an individual group in getGroupIdsWithViewPermission
findings.body: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() iterates all resources of type Groups using resourceStore.findByType. This includes the resource-type resource named Groups created by AdminPermissionsSchema.init. The loop treats it as an individual group, so an all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS or MANAGE_MEMBERS permission can cause the type resource identifier to be added to the set of group IDs used for user searches. The type-level resource should be skipped or handled as an all-groups case.

findings.title: getResourceName does not resolve Groups resources
findings.body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName() only special-cases the Users resource type. For Groups resources, whose resource name is the group ID and which are created without a useful display name, it falls back to resource.getDisplayName(), which will be null or the raw ID. This can cause admin UI/API responses for permissions referencing groups to show no meaningful name. A branch should resolve GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE resources to the group name or path.

findings.title: Possible NullPointerException in getScope for invalid resource type
findings.body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getScope() calls SCHEMA.getResourceTypes().get(resourceType).getScopes() when the authorization schema is supported. If resourceType is null or not one of the known types, get() returns null and the subsequent getScopes() throws NullPointerException instead of returning a validation error. This can turn malformed or unsupported input into a 500 error.

findings.title: Group removal listener can call unsupported V2 method
findings.body: AdminPermissions.registerListener() still calls management(...).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false) on GroupRemovedEvent. When the V2 evaluator is selected, GroupPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException. If the V1 fine-grained authz feature is enabled alongside V2, group removal events can fail during listener processing. The V2 implementation should no-op or the listener should account for V2.

findings.title: Removing global canView short-circuit forces per-group authorization checks
findings.body: GroupsResource.getGroups now filters every returned group with groupsEvaluator::canView instead of first checking groupsEvaluator.canView() and skipping per-item checks when global view is available. In V2, each canView(group) can perform resource lookups and policy evaluation; for large group listings with an all-groups permission this may significantly increase latency. The same pattern was applied in GroupResource.getSubGroups.
